files.content:
---
name: browser-capture
description: Capture URLs, inspect DOM and styles, take screenshots, and QA rendered pages with a browser-first tool ladder (Agentlas Browser -> Chrome -> Playwright). Use when a task needs rendered-page evidence, visual QA of a local preview, or screenshot proof before a design or build handoff.
---

# Browser Capture

A capability skill for browser-required work: capturing a page as evidence,
inspecting what actually rendered, and producing screenshot proof for QA.

## Tool ladder (in order — do not skip levels)

1. **Agentlas Browser** — first choice for URL capture, DOM/style inspection,
   screenshots, and local preview verification.
2. **Chrome (CDP)** — fallback when the Agentlas Browser cannot access or
   capture the target (auth-gated pages the user is signed into, extensions).
3. **Playwright** — automation fallback only, and only after the user approves
   running scripted automation against the target.

## Capture rules

- Capture the page as the user would see it: real viewport, real theme, after
  network settles. A screenshot taken mid-load is not evidence.
- For visual QA, capture BOTH desktop and mobile widths before judging layout.
- When comparing an implementation against a design target, put the capture and
  the target side by side and name concrete differences (spacing, color, type,
  overflow) — "looks close" is not a QA verdict.
- Console errors count as findings even when the page looks right.

## Evidence discipline

- Save captures with names that say what they prove (`pricing-mobile-375.png`,
  not `screenshot2.png`).
- Never hotlink or re-serve third-party source assets from a capture.
- Never include credentials, private account data, or machine-local paths in
  shared captures or reports.

See `references/qa-checklist.md` for the pre-handoff checklist.

# Rendered-page QA checklist

Run through this before calling a page "verified":

- [ ] Page loads with no console errors (warnings noted).
- [ ] Desktop width (>=1280) — no horizontal scroll, no overlapping elements.
- [ ] Mobile width (375) — nav usable, text legible, tap targets reachable.
- [ ] Light and dark theme both painted deliberately (no host-bleed backgrounds).
- [ ] Interactive elements respond (hover/focus states exist where expected).
- [ ] Screenshots saved with descriptive names and attached to the report.
- [ ] Differences against the design target listed concretely, or "none found".

defaultPrompts: Capture this preview URL and QA the mobile layout
Screenshot the pricing page in light and dark theme
